lines.text: For almost thirty years, the internet has been furious at a piece of wood.
There was room on that door.
So people tested it. In pools. In labs. On television.
And they all found the same thing. The door fits two. It just can't float two.
Unless you change one small thing. This is Titanic. Where Jack lives.
Two and a half miles down, a treasure hunter opens a rusted safe. No diamond. Just a drawing, of a young woman wearing one.
Then the phone rings. A woman who is one hundred years old.
The woman in the picture is me.
Southampton, nineteen twelve. The largest moving object ever built is about to leave on its first voyage.
Rose boards in first class, engaged to Cal, a man who treats her like something he bought.
Jack Dawson boards with five minutes to spare, on a ticket he just won at poker.
He has ten dollars, a sketchbook, and the best view on the ship.
I'm the king of the world!
That night, Rose runs to the very back of the ship, and climbs over the rail. Jack talks her back.
You jump, I jump.
As a thank you, he is invited to dinner in first class. He borrows a tuxedo, and survives it.
Then he shows her a real party. Below decks. Fiddles, beer, and dancing until the floor shakes.
At sunset, on the bow, she steps up onto the rail, and opens her arms.
I'm flying, Jack!
She asks him to draw her, wearing the Heart of the Ocean. He signs it. April fourteenth.
It is the last calm hour the ship will ever have.
Eleven forty at night. Flat sea. No moon. Two lookouts, and no binoculars.
Iceberg, right ahead!
The ship turns. Not fast enough. The ice opens the hull, like a zipper.
The designer does the math. She can float with four compartments flooded. Not five. She has about two hours.
There are more than two thousand people on board. And lifeboats for about half.
Cal plants the diamond on Jack. Jack is handcuffed to a pipe, deep in the ship, and the water is rising.
Rose has a seat in a lifeboat. She gives it up, finds an axe, and goes back down.
I'm not leaving without you.
The band keeps playing. The lights stay on almost to the end. Then they go out, all at once.
The stern rises out of the sea. The ship breaks in two. Jack and Rose ride the last of it down.
The water is below freezing. Fifteen hundred people are in it. Most have minutes.
Jack finds a carved wooden panel, and gets Rose onto it. He tries to climb on. It tips. So he stays in the water.
In the movie, he makes her promise to survive. And by the time a boat comes back, he is gone.
That is the ending you know.
Here is the one where the door fits two.
The door was never too small. It just sat too low. With two people on it, it sinks under the surface, and they both freeze.
So in our version, Rose stops him. She takes off her lifejacket.
And she ties it underneath the door.
It is the fix that every test agrees on. The door rides higher. It holds. And Jack climbs out of the water.
You jump, I jump. Remember?
They hold on to each other. They keep each other talking. They do not fall asleep.
And then, across the dark, a single lifeboat comes back.
Is anyone alive out there?
Rose finds a whistle. And blows.
At dawn, a rescue ship arrives. Seven hundred survivors. This time, two of them are sharing one blanket.
Cal walks the deck, looking for her. She pulls the blanket over both their heads.
New York, in the rain. Under the Statue of Liberty, an officer asks for her name.
Dawson. Rose Dawson.
And the man next to her gives the same one.
In her coat pocket, she finds the diamond. They are free, they are broke, and they are alive.
But here is the thing nobody says about the door.
Jack dying is what made it a perfect love story. Four days. No rent. No arguments. Frozen forever, at its very best.
Alive, it has to become a real one.
They ride the roller coaster in Santa Monica. They ride horses in the surf. Everything he promised.
Then comes a cold apartment. Burnt dinners. His drawings sell for a nickel. They fight about money.
And every time it gets bad enough, one of them says the same four words.
You jump, I jump.

lines.text: Eighty four years later, an old woman walks to the stern of a research ship, holding a diamond.
In the movie, she is alone.
In ours, there are footsteps behind her.
You're going to catch cold, Rose.
They never sold it. They never needed to. They let it go together.
And the door? It is in a museum now. The plaque reads: capacity, two.
So. Would Jack and Rose have lasted? Comment forever, or four days.
And tell us what to reimagine next.
The Matrix, where Neo takes the blue pill? The Dark Knight, where the Joker tells the truth? Or Jurassic Park, where the fences hold?
The top comment gets made. And send this to the friend who still says there was room.
